 ATP Paris Best Bets Including Alejandro Tabilo Vs Rafael Jodar 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The ATP Paris Masters tournament begins in France. This is the last 1,000-point tournament of the year and is the last regular tour event of the tennis season for most of the top pros other than the eight men who qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy. The Davis Cup is later in November, but that’s not a regular tour stop. For a lot of tennis players, this week in the City of Light is the finale for the calendar year, a final chance to bank significant points and prize money going into the offseason. This is always an interesting tournament because every player competing in Paris knows this is it for the year. Even the players who advance to the ATP Finals can really pour themselves into the action in France, because they get a week off before the ATP Finals begin. Whatever is left in the tank gets emptied this week. It makes for interesting matches and an ample supply of drama.
 The 2026 ATP Paris tournament features a scramble for the last few spots in Turin. Four spots have been clinched and four spots are left. Fifth-place Flavio Cobolli and sixth-place Arthur Fils own very strong positions for Turin. They haven’t officially clinched, but it will be very hard for either of them to get knocked out of the year-end championship showcase in Italy. Frances Tiafoe is in seventh place. He’s not a lock for Turin, but he does have a lead of close to 200 points in the race over Alex De Minaur and Rafael Jodar, who are neck and neck in the battle for the eighth and final spot in Turin. De Minaur, as a top-eight seed, gets a bye into the Round of 32 whereas Jodar must play a Round of 64 match, so that one detail instantly gives De Minaur a slight edge. If Jodar loses in the Round of 64, he’s done.
 Trailing De Minaur and Jodar are Novak Djokovic, Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul. All three must make the semifinals just to have a chance going into this weekend. Paul must make the final and get help. In all likelihood, any of the three in this group need to make the final and get help from De Minaur or Jodar’s opponents in France. When the week ends, we’ll know who is heading to Turin. LWOS has our best bets for three matches. Post your best bets and thoughts in the comments.
 ATP Paris 
 Alejandro Tabilo – Rafael Jodar: 6:30 EST 
 H2H: 1-3 
 This ATP Paris match is a featured attraction due to the ATP Finals stakes attached to it. Rafael Jodar almost certainly has to win this match to have any chance of advancing to Italy for the year-end championship event. He is 3-2 in his last five matches while his opponent, Alejandro Tabilo, is 1-4.
 Best Bet to Make 
 Welcome to our best bet section. You’re going to get a collection of bets to consider, also a confidence level which should guide how much you should invest in this match. 
 Parlay/hedge options: none 
 Confidence level on a scale of 1-10: 7 – You could bet three fourths of a unit on this match.  
 This ATP Paris match sets up extremely well for Jodar. He has all the motivation while Tabilo is not in good form. This points to Jodar in straights.
 That being said, betting on Jodar -1.5 sets is the best bet you can make 
 Value bet/ the best odds: Jodar -1.5 sets at 1.71 at @1xbet 
 Casper Ruud – Juan Manuel Cerundolo: 8:00 EST 
 H2H: 1-2 
 This ATP Paris match is a reunion of players who met twice earlier in 2026, splitting their two matches. Casper Ruud beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo in Montreal. Cerundolo beat Ruud in Gstaad. Let’s see how they match up on an indoor hardcourt.
 May 28, 2024; Paris,, France; Casper Ruud of Norway returns a shot during his match against Felipe Meligeni Alves of Brazil on day three of Roland Garros at Stade Roland Garros. Mandatory Credit: Susan Mullane-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith 
 Best Bet to Make 
 Parlay/hedge options: Cerundolo +1.5 sets at 1.80 at @betway 
 Confidence level on a scale of 1-10: 7 – you could bet three fourths of a unit on this match. 
 This ATP Paris match lines up well for Ruud, who was easily better on hardcourts in Montreal (6-1 6-2) and has seen Cerundolo up close in two matches this year. Ruud adjusted to the Gstaad loss when he faced Cerundolo in Montreal. Ruud should be able to maintain the upper hand. We feel confident about that.
 That being said, betting on Ruud -2.5 games is the best bet you can make 
 Value bet/ the best odds: Ruud -2.5 games at 1.60 at @1xbet 
 Cameron Norrie – Matteo Arnaldi: 8:00 EST 
 H2H: 0-1 
 This ATP Paris match is a hard one to call, and the backdrop to the match includes the fact that both players are playing poorly. They are both 1-4 in their last five matches.
 Best Bet to Make 
 Parlay/hedge options: Arnaldi +1.5 sets at 1.73 at @betway, over 2.5 sets at 2.40 at @betway 
 Confidence level on a scale of 1-10: 1 – you should not bet on this match. 
 This ATP Paris match is a terrible match to bet on. You never bet on two bad teams or two struggling athletes, because a bad team or struggling athlete has not shown any trustworthy characteristics. You want to trust teams or athletes which can be trusted. You can fade a bad team if it is playing a superior opponent, but when two bad teams or athletes are going against each other, there’s no one to trust. If you insist on a bet, we will lean to Norrie, but really, this is a match to sit out.
 That being said, betting on Norrie -2.5 games is the best bet you can make 
 Value bet/ the best odds: Norrie -2.5 games at 1.70 @interwetten
